maya: Hey — background-sync job (worker pool) traces show the root span in jaeger but almost none of the child spans from the threaded tasks. Happens intermittently on prod, less often in staging. Anyone seen async propagation get lost like this?

sam: Can you drop a trace id or a link to the trace? also which runtime (python/node/java) and how are tasks dispatched (threadpool/processpool/child worker)?

maya: Trace id: 9f7a2c4b1d3e8f00. Link: https://dash.redwood.ai/d/trace/view?trace=9f7a2c4b1d3e8f00. Using Python 3.11, ThreadPoolExecutor from concurrent.futures inside our background-sync service. We submit HTTP calls to downstream internal service. Logs show many spans created in the main thread but child threads show no span_id/parent in jaeger.

sam: quick log snippet? even something showing headers or missing parent would help

maya: paste logs:
```
[2026-03-18T09:12:45Z] INFO sync.job: starting batch batch_id=42 trace_id=9f7a2c4b1d3e8f00 span_id=5a1b2c3d parent_span_id=null
[2026-03-18T09:12:46Z] INFO worker.thread-7: http.request url=/internal/fetch batch_id=42 trace_id=9f7a2c4b1d3e8f00 span_id=null parent_span_id=null
```

infra-bot: Incident alert: trace-rate-anomaly on background-sync (rule: missing-child-spans). Playbook: https://runbooks.redwood.ai/obs/trace-missing-children

leo: Two things to check quickly: 1) propagators config (we want W3C traceparent), and 2) context propagation across thread boundaries — contextvars don't flow into raw ThreadPoolExecutor tasks automatically. Try setting OTEL_PROPAGATORS=tracecontext and ensure your instrumentation wraps submissions.

leo: Example wrapper we use for ThreadPoolExecutor to capture context:
```
from opentelemetry import context

def wrap_with_ctx(fn, ctx):
    def inner(*a, **k):
        token = context.attach(ctx)
        try:
            return fn(*a, **k)
        finally:
            context.detach(token)
    return inner

ctx = context.get_current()
executor.submit(wrap_with_ctx(worker_task, ctx), *args)
```

ash: Also check the outgoing HTTP client: if the traceparent header isn't being forwarded into the session or is overwritten by a connection pool, child spans won't correlate. For requests, make sure the instrumentation is applied or you add the header explicitly when creating sessions. Watch for libraries that re-create connections (urllib3 pools) and strip headers.

jordan: Sampling note: if you're using a parent-based sampler wrongly configured, children could be dropped. Confirm envs: OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER=parentbased_traceidratio and OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER_ARG=0.05 (or use parentbased_always_on for repro). For quick debug set OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER=always_on to rule out sampling.

sam: Another quick repro: start a local worker with debug logging, wrap the submit, and log context in the child task (span context.trace_id, span context.span_id) before making the HTTP call. If trace id is missing in the child, wrap as Leo suggested. Also confirm OPENTELEMETRY SDK version — some older versions had context propagation bugs on Py3.11 threadlocals.

maya: Thanks — I pushed a quick patch wrapping submissions and toggled OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER=always_on in staging. Will run a canary now.

(15m later) maya: Canary looks good — child spans now present and correlated. Repro steps: added the wrap_with_ctx helper around executor.submit and set OTEL_PROPAGATORS=tracecontext. No code in downstream needed. I'll open a small PR with the wrapper and a unit test.

sam: Nice! can you include a line in the PR description about why ThreadPoolExecutor needs explicit context wrapping and link the runbook? saves future debugging. :thumbsup:

maya: Will do, PR in a few. Thanks all.
